meta.name: Little Caesars
meta.disclaimer_extra: Little Caesars publishes its nutrition as a scanned flyer, not a data file, so these figures were read off it by hand. It publishes whole pizzas; every pizza row here is that figure divided by the eight slices they cut, and toppings are the chain's own note: "amounts shown are the highest count for each topping".
meta.blurb: Little Caesars is the one big pizza chain that still publishes nutrition as a scanned flyer, which is why almost nobody has put its numbers in a calculator. Its per-topping table adds onto a cheese base, so a Detroit-Style deep dish can be built topping by topping and then cut into the slices you actually eat.

categories.name: Pizza Base
categories.note: A base is the cheese pizza — sauce and cheese included. Only these two crusts have a published topping table; thin and pretzel are whole pizzas under menu items.

categories.name: Toppings
categories.note: These are the largest portion Little Caesars puts on, so a pizza built here can come out above the same one on their menu.

ranch.reason: The flyer prints 32 g sugar against 4 g total carbohydrate for this dip, and sugar cannot exceed the carbohydrate it is part of. Buffalo Ranch — the same dressing with hot sauce — prints 3 g against the same 4 g of carbohydrate, so that is the figure used. Its 48 mg sodium is left exactly as printed: low for a dressing, but nothing in the row contradicts it.

portion_split.reason: Little Caesars publishes this per whole pizza; divided by the eight slices they cut it into, so a slice can be added to a meal the way Domino's and Papa John's already are. Both figures are theirs — eight of these is the pizza they print.
